Looks good to me is a sentence, not a review.
Running on fumes. Coffee number two, the one that actually does the work.
Lunch can be a liquid if you believe in yourself.
Leftovers. Yesterday's me was looking out for today's me, for once.
Ate at the counter, standing up, reading a changelog. Living the dream.

beats.lead: Back to work. One thing, start to finish.

Fine. Swipe them, or turn on do not disturb and enjoy the quiet.
Nine apps want my attention and none of them are getting a raise for it.

dialogue: Do not disturb is on. That sound gets through anyway. It's supposed to.
Checkout is slow at a cheese curd shop. Somewhere, a person is waiting on a button.
You build it, you carry the pager for it. Going in.

beats.objective: Find what made the click slow
dialogue: The average looks fine. The average always looks fine.
Seven components touched that click. One of them is lying.
Don't guess. Measure, then be smug.

dialogue: Send the order first, celebrate after. A two line change and a long afternoon.
Pipeline's running. This is the part where I stare at a progress bar like it owes me money.
Green. A real green this time, one I actually caused.

beats.objective: Evening's yours. Side quests, or nothing at all.

task.hint: When I'm done wandering, the write-up's waiting at the desk.

dialogue: Laptop's closed. It's still looking at me though.
There's a docs PR open on the monitor if I feel like being useful for free.
The plant has been very patient today.
If it isn't written down, it didn't happen. And it'll happen again.
What broke and why, then what we changed. Nobody gets blamed, apart from one confetti cannon.
Making it fast is half the job. Proving why is the half people skip.
Phone goes on the charger, face down, like it's in trouble.

sideQuests.title: The docs PR
sideQuests.objective: Review a docs PR on the monitor
intro: An open source project I use has a docs PR waiting. Somebody fixed an example that never ran.
Nobody gets promoted for reading docs PRs. I read them anyway.

choice.prompt: The example in the PR calls a function the library removed two versions ago. What do you do?

options.reply: Nicer wording, same broken example. That one's on me.

options.text: Run the example first, then comment with the fix.
options.reply: Ran it, it threw, left the working version in a comment. Ten minutes well spent.

options.text: Close the tab and feel bad later.
options.reply: Closed the tab. The tab knows what I did.

sideQuests.title: Answer the maintainer
intro: A maintainer left a comment on my pull request. Four words: can you add a test.
They're right. They're usually right, it's very annoying.

options.text: Add the test, push, say thanks.
options.reply: Test added. It failed first, which is how I know it's a real one.

options.text: Explain at length why it doesn't need one.
options.reply: Six paragraphs. They replied with a thumbs up and the same request.
They don't have my machine. Fair point, well made.

sideQuests.title: Water the plant
intro: The plant. Longest running thing in this house with zero monitoring.
It droops, I water it. That's the whole alerting setup.
done: Watered. It doesn't say thanks. It also never pages me.

whiteboard.title: Whiteboard
whiteboard.how: Drag the boxes on. Drag from one box to another to connect them. Then send traffic.

cdn.label: CDN
cdn.hint: Serves the files that don't change, from somewhere close.

loadBalancer.label: Load balancer
loadBalancer.hint: Spreads requests so no one box takes all of it.

app2.label: App (second copy)
app2.hint: Same code, for when the first one's busy or dead.

cache.label: Cache
cache.hint: Remembers answers so the database doesn't have to.

queue.label: Queue
queue.hint: Holds work for later so the request doesn't wait on it.

worker.label: Worker
worker.hint: Does the slow jobs off to the side.

database.label: Database
database.hint: The one thing you can't lose.

puzzles.title: Get the page to the person
puzzles.brief: A small shop goes online. 200 people show up at once. Don't let the browser near the database.

forbidden.text: The browser is talking straight to the database. Someone typed a quote mark into the search box and now there's no products table.
The CDN cached the database. All of it. Everyone's seeing one customer's order from last Tuesday.

missing.text: No CDN in front. Every image came from one box in a closet. It lasted nine seconds.
The CDN has nothing behind it. Very fast delivery of a blank page.
The app can't reach the database. It's serving the shop from memory, and its memory is bad.

puzzles.success: Held. Boring, which is the highest praise a system can get.

puzzles.title: Sale day
puzzles.brief: Everything's 30% off and the email just went out. 5,000 people, same product page. One app box isn't going to make it.

forbidden.text: Browser straight to the database again. We've talked about this.
The CDN skips the load balancer and sends everything to one app. That app has left the building.
The cache is wired to the database with nobody in charge of what goes in it. It's now confidently serving last week's prices.

missing.text: The second app's just sitting there with no traffic. The first one took all 5,000 and fell over politely.
The second app's doing everything while the first one watches. It didn't hold.
No cache on the first app. It asked the database for the same product page 5,000 times and the database stopped answering.
The second app has no cache. Half the requests are fast and the other half are killing the database.
The first app can't reach the database. Cache misses turn into error pages.
The second app can't reach the database. Every other refresh is an error. Customers think it's a game.
Nothing connects the front door to the apps. Great looking page, no shop behind it.
No CDN. The apps spent the whole sale serving the logo.

puzzles.success: It held, and the database barely noticed. That's the cache doing its one job.

forbidden.text: The app calls the worker directly and waits. Checkout is now exactly as fast as the email service, which is not fast.
The browser's writing to the queue. Someone queued 40,000 receipts for an order that doesn't exist.
Browser to database. Every time. Why is it always this one.

missing.text: Nothing goes on the queue. Orders work, nobody gets a receipt, support gets all of it.
The queue fills up and nobody's reading it. 12,000 emails, waiting, forever.
The app took the order and didn't write it down anywhere. Fast though.
The load balancer has nothing to balance.
Nobody can get in. Zero errors. Zero orders too.

puzzles.success: Checkout answered right away and the emails went out when they went out. Nobody waits on a receipt.

diffs.title: Add a seconds counter
diffs.explanation: The interval keeps the count from the first render, so it sets 1 forever. Use setCount(c => c + 1).

diffs.title: Load the user for the profile card
diffs.explanation: The effect reads userId but never re-runs when it changes, so the card keeps showing the first user.

diffs.title: Sort tickets by priority
diffs.kind: index as key on a reordered list
diffs.explanation: The list gets reordered, so an index key hands each row's typed draft to whichever ticket lands in that slot. Key on ticket.id.

diffs.title: Show a toast when the order saves
diffs.explanation: The post isn't awaited, so it says Saved before the request finishes and the catch never sees a failure.

diffs.title: Paginate the orders table
lines: for (let i = start; i <= end; i++) {
diffs.explanation: The loop includes end, so every page has one row too many and the last page ends in undefined. It should be i < end.
diffs.fix: for (let i = start; i < end; i++) {

diffs.title: Add a sort button to the leaderboard
diffs.explanation: sort changes the array in place and returns the same one, so React sees no change and the parent's data got reordered too. Copy it first.

hunt.title: The hunt
hunt.how: Read the clue, rule out suspects, then name the one that made the click slow. A wrong accusation costs time.

shop.name: Squeaky Curd Outfitters
shop.tagline: Cheese curds, shipped cold, to people who can't wait.
shop.note: Made up. Any resemblance to a real cheese shop is a coincidence and a compliment.

incident.title: Checkout is slow
incident.summary: Customers click Place order and nothing happens for over a second. Then they click it again.

suspects.label: <CurdCarousel>
suspects.desc: Spins product photos up top. Very proud of itself.
suspects.alibi: It's above the fold and wasn't touched by the click.

suspects.label: <ChatBubble>
suspects.desc: A support widget that says hi every 30 seconds.
suspects.alibi: It runs on a timer. The click barely waited before its handler started.

suspects.label: <CouponField>
suspects.alibi: It only does work when you type in it. Nobody typed.

suspects.label: <ShippingEstimator>
suspects.desc: Guesses how long cold cheese takes to cross the country.
suspects.alibi: It did its work on the address step. It was idle during the click.

suspects.label: <CartSummary>
suspects.alibi: It re-rendered once, in 6 ms. That's allowed.

suspects.label: <PlaceOrderButton>
suspects.alibi: It's where the click landed, not where the time went. It just passes the click along.

suspects.label: <CurdConfetti>
suspects.desc: Throws tiny cheese curds across the screen when you order. Added last week.

clues.text: Input delay was 38 ms. The page wasn't busy when the click arrived.
clues.meaning: So nothing running in the background held the click up.

clues.text: Processing took 1,012 ms. Nearly all the time went into the click's own handlers.
clues.meaning: So it's something that runs because of this click, not something that ran earlier.

clues.text: During that click one component mounted 4,000 children. Another re-rendered once, in 6 ms.
clues.meaning: Adding up a cart doesn't take 4,000 anything.

wrongGuess: Not that one. It's got an alibi, read it.
Guessing is how two teams end up both claiming the fix.
Nope. The numbers don't point there.

lines: what           mounted 4,000 confetti curds before sending the order
note           The order had not been sent yet. It celebrated first.
readout.verdict: It's <CurdConfetti>. Somebody throws a party on the main thread before the order even leaves the building.
readout.fixHint: Send the order first. Then confetti, a lot less of it, after the next paint.

hunt.timeout: Out of time. The readout names it anyway, the tool's faster than I am today.
solved: Confetti. A second of everyone's life, per order, for confetti.
Nobody's in trouble. The confetti's in trouble.
